# Baruch Chapter 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Baruch 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/BAR_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1** And these are the words of the book which Baruch son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, son of Zedekiah, son of Hasadiah, son of Hilkiah, wrote in Babylon,

**2** in the fifth year, on the seventh day of the month, at the time when the Chaldeans took Jerusalem and burned it with fire.

**3** And Baruch read the words of this book in the hearing of Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and in the hearing of all the people who came to hear the book,

**4** and in the hearing of the mighty ones, and of the sons of kings, and of the elders, and in the hearing of all the people, from the least to the greatest, all who were dwelling in Babylon by the River Sud.

**5** And they wept and fasted and prayed before the Lord.

**6** And they collected money, each according to his power,

**7** and they sent it to Jerusalem to Jehoiakim the priest, son of Hilkiah, son of Shallum, and to the priests and to all the people who were found with him in Jerusalem,

**8** when he received the vessels of the house of the Lord that had been carried away from the temple, to return them to the land of Judah, on the tenth of Sivan — the silver vessels that Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, had made,

**9** after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away Jeconiah and the leaders and the captives and the mighty men and the people of the land from Jerusalem and brought them to Babylon.

**10** And they said: Behold, we send you money; buy with the money burnt offerings and sin offerings and incense, and prepare a grain offering, and offer them upon the altar of the Lord our God;

**11** and pray for the life of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and for the life of his son Belshazzar, that their days upon the earth may be as the days of heaven.

**12** And the Lord will give us strength, and he will enlighten our eyes, and we shall live under the shadow of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and under the shadow of his son Belshazzar, and we shall serve them many days and find favor in their sight.

**13** And pray for us to the Lord our God, for we have sinned against the Lord our God, and the anger of the Lord and his wrath have not turned away from us to this day.

**14** And you shall read this book which we have sent to you, to make confession in the house of the Lord on the day of the feast and on the days of the appointed seasons.

**15** And you shall say: To the Lord our God belongs righteousness, but to us shame of face, as it is this day, to the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem,

**16** and to our kings and our rulers and our priests and our prophets and our fathers,

**17** because we sinned before the Lord

**18** and disobeyed him and did not listen to the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in the commandments of the Lord which he set before us.

**19** From the day when the Lord brought our fathers out of the land of Egypt until this day, we have been disobedient to the Lord our God, and we have been negligent in not listening to his voice.

**20** And there clung to us the calamities and the curse which the Lord commanded through Moses his servant, from the day when he brought our fathers out of the land of Egypt to give us a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is this day.

**21** And we did not listen to the voice of the Lord our God, according to all the words of the prophets whom he sent to us,

**22** and each of us went after the inclinations of his own evil heart, to serve other gods and to do what is evil in the sight of the Lord our God.

---
*EMET renders the Greek of Vaticanus closely. v.8 "on the tenth of Sivan" follows the Greek text as given. v.11 retains the political prayer for the pagan king as theologically notable. v.20 "calamities" renders ta kaka; "curse" renders the oath/imprecation formula.*
